I have nothing against weed itself. But this thread alone shows a lot of the problems with it. The main one is lots of forms of denial.

Key Problems: a) People who smoke often are in denial about it's effects on the brain / body. It is safer than alcohol, yes, but there should be like 100 footnotes after that. The biggest "safety" misconception is equating smoking to binge drinking. The problem is the average smoker will smoke multiple times a week or sometimes multiple times a day but most people that drink may drink moderate amounts on an average weekend and maybe get drunk a few times a month or year, depending on age.

b) Separate from the denial of the effects are the actual effects. Chronic users have slower brain function. That doesn't mean they are not smart or even smarter than me. What it means is they are slower than when they are off the drug and are generally more lazy, more ok with failure, etc. A lot of success in life can be had by just spending every minute of every day doing something productive. Being proud of what you have accomplished generates far more happiness than hiding behind a drug.

c) Stereotypes that are generally adopted by smokers. I think this is unrelated to the weed and is more a "fitting in" thing. People who smoke just start to approach life differently and to non-regular smokers it is annoying.

d) Denial of the habit forming nature of usage. It is not "medically" addicting in the sense that that are no physical withdrawal symptoms. That said, tell someone to stop and they will make up a million excuses of why they CAN but DON'T WANT TO. Of course you can, just like I can become a millionaire. [Combine this with point A above and you get a shit storm]

e) Cost. If you can afford it, no problem. But too many people are spending what very little money they have on this expensive product that does not really benefit them the way it could if they purchased other products or saved for retirement.

f) Peer pressure. Smokers NEVER want to smoke alone and will try to recruit more smokers to make themselves feel better about smoking all the time. I had a roommate who smoked every day, multiple times, and every time he lit up he asked me if I wanted to. Every smoker I knew did not like non-smokers hanging around when they smoked unless it was the "I have a drug test" excuse. If you don't want to smoke they have some derogatory thing to say or they talk about how safe it is or whatever.
